nodes.name: Ag Doping of h-BN Monolayer
nodes.procedure: Pristine h-BN monolayer (3×3×1 supercell with 9 B and 9 N atoms, 15 Å vacuum layer) constructed and geometry optimized using DMol3/CASTEP with GGA-PBE/DNP/DFT-D/DSPP. Three Ag doping sites tested: (1) above six-membered ring center (E_b = -1.004 eV), (2) above N atom (E_b = -0.987 eV), (3) above B atom (E_b = -0.977 eV, Ag-B = 2.870 Å). Site above B atom selected as most stable based on shortest Ag-hBN distance and binding energy analysis.

unit_operations.name: h-BN Construction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: choose 3×3×1 cells to construct h-BN, which contains 9 B atoms and 9 N atoms. In order to avoid interference in the z-axis direction, we set a vacuum layer of 15Å

unit_operations.name: DFT Geometry Optimization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: DFT-based calculations performed in Dmol3 and CASTEP modules of MS software... The energy tolerance accuracy, the maximum force, and the displacement are set to 1×10^{-5} Ha, 2×10^{-3} Ha/Å, and 5×10^{-3} Å

unit_operations.name: Ag Doping Site Screening
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Ag atom placed above the six-membered ring center, Ag atom above the N atom, and Ag atom above the B atom... the binding energies in the three cases are -1.004 eV, -0.987 eV, and -0.977 eV respectively

nodes.source_text: First, we choose 3×3×1 cells to construct h-BN... the binding energies in the three cases are -1.004 eV, -0.987 eV, and -0.977 eV respectively. The binding energy also confirms our conclusion that the Ag atom above the B atom is the optimal structure

nodes.description: DFT computational testing of gas adsorption and sensing performance for NO2, SO2F2, and NO
nodes.source_text: The adsorption energies of NO2, SO2F2, and NO adsorption systems were -1.893 eV, -1.361 eV, and -0.817 eV, respectively... the gas sensing performance is SO2F2 > NO2 > NO... The results showed that the sensitivities of NO2 and SO2F2 were very high at different temperatures, with the highest values of 5.70×10^12 and 6.97×10^28, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT geometry optimization identifies Ag above B atom as optimal doping site with Ag-N distance 2.870 Å and binding energy -0.977 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: when the Ag atom is placed above B atom, the distance between Ag atom and N atom below is 2.870Å ... the binding energies in the three cases are -1.004eV, -0.987eV, and -0.977eV respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bandgap decreases from 4.658 eV (pristine h-BN) to 0.537 eV after Ag doping, with denser band structure indicating improved conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: before and after doping, the h-BN monolayer changed greatly, band gap energy decreased from 4.658eV to 0.537eV, and the energy band curve became denser.

nodes.characterization_summary: TDOS of Ag-BN monolayer is left-shifted with higher electron distribution near Fermi level compared to pristine h-BN, indicating improved conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the TDOS of the Ag-BN monolayer is significantly left-shifted compared with that of the pristine h-BN monolayer ... indicating that the conductivity of the substrate is improved after Ag doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: Adsorption energies are -1.893 eV for NO2, -1.361 eV for SO2F2, and -0.817 eV for NO, indicating adsorption between physical and chemical adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the adsorption energies of NO2, SO2F2, and NO adsorption systems were -1.893eV, -1.361eV, and -0.817eV, respectively ... these three adsorption systems are between physical adsorption and chemical adsorption.

nodes.characterization_summary: Negative charge transfers indicate electrons transfer from Ag-BN to gases, with gas sensing performance SO2F2 > NO2 > NO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the transfer charge of the three adsorption systems is negative ... from the perspective of charge transfer, the gas sensing properties of the Ag-BN monolayer for three gases are SO2F2 > NO2 > NO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge density difference shows large charge distribution around gas and Ag atoms, confirming strong adsorption interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: there is a large amount of charge distribution around the gas and Ag atoms, indicating that the adsorption between gas molecules and the Ag-BN monolayer is obvious.
